**Syllabus** [PDF](syllabus.pdf)

STAT:5400 Computing in Statistics is a required course for first-year master's students in statistics and data science. Through hands-on work on real problems, it develops the computing skills that applied statistics and research in statistical methodology and theory depend on.

The course has two components.

- **Statistical computing methods**: generating random variables, Monte Carlo studies, resampling methods, computing linear models, computation for high-dimensional statistics, machine learning algorithms, and large language models.
- **Tech guide**: the tools of reproducible statistical work — Linux, Git and GitHub, R Markdown and Quarto, writing R packages, C and Fortran from R, parallel computing, and working with large language models through APIs and R packages.

**What makes this course different**

- **AI from the first week.** LLMs are used to brainstorm, as a tutor, and for vibe coding. You will also call AI from R and Python the way a statistician would: as something to sample from and to evaluate.
- **Bilingual.** Examples and assignments in both R and Python.
- **Interactive notes.** Most examples run right in the browser, with nothing to install. Examples that need a real machine (a compiler, an API key, more memory) open in a GitHub Codespace, or you can run them on your own computer.
- **Real tools.** Git and GitHub, Codespaces, Copilot, Linux, R packages.

_Notes will be added section by section during the semester._
